title: Chicken breast, baked, broiled, or roasted, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken breast is a lean source of protein obtained by baking, broiling, or roasting. The meat is tender, low in fat, and commonly used in health‑focused diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides more protein per 100 g than most other meat cuts.
When cooked without skin, the fat content drops by almost half compared with pan‑frying.
The meat is rich in vitamin B6, which plays a role in amino‑acid metabolism.
In culinary practice, breast is often marinated in lemon juice or yogurt to retain moisture.
A popular method is “en papillote” – cooking the breast in parchment with herbs to lock in flavor and juices.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: With about 31 g of protein per 100 g, it supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Skinless breast contains less than 3 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B6 and niacin aid energy metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: Protein digests slowly, helping to maintain fullness longer.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken meat.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Pre‑made marinades can be high in salt; monitor sodium intake if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the breast for salads, sandwiches, stir‑fries, or serve it whole with vegetable sides. Marinating in lemon, olive oil and herbs before baking enhances juiciness and flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh breast in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Freeze at –18 °C for up to 9 months. Thaw in the fridge rather than at room temperature before cooking.
